short: How much demand changes when you change the price.
seoTitle: Price Elasticity — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: Price elasticity of demand measures how much the quantity sold changes when the price changes. Elasticity decides where to raise prices.
definition: Price elasticity of demand measures how much the quantity sold changes when the price changes. Elastic items lose volume quickly when prices rise; inelastic ones barely move, which is where price increases are safest.
bodyHtml:
Why Price Elasticity matters

Elasticity decides where to raise prices. Signature dishes, staples and convenience purchases usually absorb a rise; commodity items that customers can price-compare do not.

Price Elasticity formula

Elasticity = % change in quantity sold ÷ % change in price

A result beyond −1 means demand is elastic and revenue falls when prices rise.

How Price Elasticity works in practice

You rarely need a formal figure. Raise the price of one item, watch volume for a few weeks against a comparable item you left alone, and let the result guide the next change.

Worked example

A 10% price rise that costs 4% of volume is inelastic, so revenue and margin both improve.

faq.question: Which menu items can I reprice safely?
faq.answer: Popular items with no close comparison elsewhere, and low-cost add-ons, tend to be the least sensitive.

faq.question: How often should prices change?
faq.answer: Small, regular adjustments are absorbed far better than one large annual jump.
